movement_profile.footwork: Rhythmic stepping with emphasis on the fourth beat, light quick step (arrebato), and strong foot stamping (zapateo)
movement_profile.formation_and_space: Circular formation with four to eight dancers, moving together in coordinated patterns

signature_moves.description: A light, quick step performed within the circular formation
signature_moves.name: Arrebato

signature_moves.description: A strong foot stamping step resembling a huayno escape step, used to conclude the dance
signature_moves.name: Zapateo

movement_profile.tempo_feel: Steady rhythmic pulse with moments of light quick steps and strong stamping
movement_profile.what_to_avoid: Avoid inappropriate use of sacred masks and costumes Avoid disrespecting the ritual context

music_profile.meter: not explicitly described, implied steady rhythmic pattern with emphasis on fourth beat
music_profile.musical_form: Traditional pattern throughout dance; chuscadas for general dances
music_profile.rhythm_pattern: Traditional pattern with rhythmic support on the fourth beat; chuscadas played during general dances
music_profile.sound_description: The music features a wooden pinkullo flute with a clear, piercing tone and a large wanqar drum providing deep, resonant beats. The rhythm emphasizes the fourth beat, creating a steady, ritualistic pulse typical of northern Peruvian highlands.

basic_steps: Form a circle with fellow dancers
Step rhythmically with emphasis on the fourth beat
Perform a light, quick step called arrebato
Execute a strong zapateo foot stamping to end
teaching.formation: Circular group formation of four to eight dancers, sometimes led by a captain
teaching.level_notes: Beginners start with basic circle formation and rhythmic stepping; intermediate dancers add arrebato and zapateo steps; advanced dancers master timing and group coordination
teaching.rhythm: Rhythmic support on the fourth beat with a pattern typical of northern Peruvian highlands
